reviewer: Claude agent review (Opus), not a human historian
text: 2026-10-23: the book was rewritten to the storytelling template (README §6) and approved on an independent review against facts.json, both research files, Bühler's 1875 introduction (pp. 38–43, checked in the archive.org scan) and all thirteen pictures. Four named people (ವಿಕ್ರಮಾದಿತ್ಯ, ಸೋಮೇಶ್ವರ, ಜಯಸಿಂಹ, ಬಿಲ್ಹಣ) and three years in the prose; NFC, no em dashes; the turning point is the charge in scene 9 and the hand on the brother's shoulder follows it.

Fixed on that review: the Jayasimha battle had been told as a march toward Banavasi across an unnamed river with 'no source' for its place; Bühler (pp. 42–43) has both armies advance to the Krishna and one more attempt at talks, so the scene is now on the Krishna, f-jayasimha-clemency and research §4a carry the quotations, and Bilhana's end-1077 against Fleet's 1082 is disclosed. Also fixed: an ambiguous ಅಣ್ಣ in scene 5 that let a reader think Someshvara took the boy, an undisclosed line suggesting others turned Jayasimha, and Gangavadi called ಮಲೆನಾಡು.

Newcomer test (README §7): (1) yes, a first-time reader can say who he was (the second son who refused his brother's throne), what he wanted, what happened and why it matters; (2) yes, 'remember this boy' pays off at the forest's edge, the stakes are said before the charge, and the hand on the shoulder is the goosebump moment. The Bilhana recital placed before the revolt, the midday capture, the reordered pictures and the unnamed queen are disclosed in their scenes.

2026-10-15: approved on a third read of story.json (introduction, twelve scenes with paragraphs, alt texts, facts and dramatised lists, summary, ನಿಮಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತೇ?, visitToday, provenance, disclosure, content note), facts.json and dynasty.json, after the first pass returned sixteen text blockers and two dynasty blockers and the second pass four small text blockers and one image blocker, all now fixed.

Blockers found on the first pass and fixed: (1) ಯುವರಾಜ used for Vikrama as prince, contradicting his refusal of the post (intro, scene-02 title, summary, three facts), now ರಾಜಕುಮಾರ; (2) a coup foreshadow ('ಇನ್ನೂ.' in scene-02, 'ಅವನ ಕಣ್ಣು … ಕಲ್ಯಾಣದ ಕಡೆಗೆ' in scene-05), removed; (3) source commentary inside scenes ('ಯಾರೂ ಬರೆದಿಡಲಿಲ್ಲ', 'ತಮಿಳು ನಾಡಿನ ಕಲ್ಲುಗಳೂ', 'ಗದಗಿನ ಕಲ್ಲು ಮುಂದೆ ಹೇಳಿತು', 'ಯಾವ ಕಲ್ಲೂ ಹೇಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ', 'ಮದುವೆ ನಿಜ; ಹೂಮಾಲೆ ಕವಿಯದು', 'ಅದೇ ವರ್ಷದ ಕಲ್ಲುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ', 'ಅದು ಕಲ್ಲಿನ ಲೆಕ್ಕ', 'ಯಾರೂ ಕೆತ್ತಲಿಲ್ಲ'), now dropped or told as events (the Gadag carver of 1098); (4) scene-12 had the Kalyana throne 'returned' by 1169-70 (Someshvara IV recovered it only by 1183-84) and named Basava in a scene, now 'ಬೇರೆ ಮನೆತನದ ಕೈಗೆ ಹೋಗಿತ್ತು' with Bijjala and Basava on the last page only; (5) 'a thousand years of Saka on every stone', 'some old king's era' and 'every stone for fifty years', now the 1068 stone's Saka 990 and Fleet's 'nearly all'; (6) Permadi called a new name in 1076 (it is in Sk 136 of 1068) and 31 January 1077 called the coronation day (Fleet unsure, Bhandarkar against), now the grant day of the pattabandha festival; (7) 'his first inscription' for Sk 136; (8) Stein's modern 'ludicrous' given to Kalhana as Harsha's 'own historian', an undisclosed 'never came near Kalyana', and 'Kalyana's elephant coin' for Harsha's Karnata-type coin; (9) a Chola taunt ('ಉದ್ಧಟ') in scene prose and the poem-only second Kanchi war told without disclosure; (10) 'the emperor was not there' at Kannegal, firmer than 'not said to be present', removed; (11) Kalhana called Bilhana's townsman; (12) the Yajnavalkya commentary, 'eight centuries of courts' and the Mitakshara stanzas given to Vijnaneshvara as author (teaser, intro, scene-11), now Bhandarkar's 'chief authority over a large part of India' and stanzas that 'occur at the end of most manuscripts'; (13) Jayakarna's death before his father stated without Fleet's 'probably', now disclosed; (14) 'abolished by decree, not by enforcement' (fact and summary), removed; (15) the kingdom 'from the Narmada to the Tungabhadra' in the intro, against Gangavadi and Banavasi; (16) provenance and visitToday linked to Temple's 'India in 1880' (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.69689), now Fleet 1896. Dynasty entry: 'the greatest name' and Kalhana's 'lords of Karnata' (he names only Vikramaditya), both fixed. Second pass: a duplicated sentence in scene-07, stale dramatised entries in scene-08 and scene-11 (one claiming the prose called Bilhana's peace court praise after that line was removed), and scene-06 told at night while its picture shows daylight, now 'ಯುದ್ಧ ಮುಗಿದ ಮೇಲೆ' with the alt to match.

Every name, number, year, relationship and quotation was compared with research/kalyani-chalukya-verified.md: Taila II from 973-74 and the line to 1189; Kalyana as capital in a record of 1053 (Malkhed only Fleet's guess); the boar crest; Bachaladevi as mother of all three brothers (Gadag 1098 and 1102; Rice's Ganga mother rejected); 1055-56 Gangavadi 96,000 and Banavasi 12,000, Harikesarin, Chalukya-Ganga-Permanadi, the Permadi basadi; the yuvaraja refusal as the poem's; 29 March 1068 (Sunday, Chaitra bahula 8, Kuruvatti, supreme yoga, ascended to heaven) and the poem's fever, ministers, gold, water to the neck, waves and music; the Krishna rites and grief without the disarming; 11 April 1068, Gutti and 'Junior is king Vikrama-Ganga to me'; the break and Jayasimha taken along; Virarajendra's daughter (confirmed by SII III), Kanchi, Rajiga, with Fleet's anachronism disclosed; the alliance, two dreams, captive and hesitation, with the Gadag 'seized in battle', the Kalige 'punished or confined', Buhler's verdict and 'not known' on the last page; the first year from about 9 March 1076 (Saka 999 current) and 31 January 1077 at Nadaviyuppayana-vidu; the Yedarave 1094-95 and Gadag 1098 era lines (the Nanda doubt disclosed); the Lakshmeshwar record with Chalukya-Vikrama year 2 and Saka 1000 (the misprinted Saka 969 not quoted); Jayasimha yuvaraja at Banavasi 1077-82, Lakshmana to Rama, the war and clemency as the poem's; Chandaladevi piriyarasi and agramahamahishi, father 'probably' Narasimha, the svayamvara as the poem's; Harsha's portrait, vow and coin (Stein VII.1119-1124, VII.926; Cunningham); the Narmada in 1088-89 and 1098 with the opponent unnamed, Draksharama, the feudatories; Kannegal about 1117, twelve tributary chiefs, Achugi; 'Know the Hoysala alone … unconquerable' in Bhandarkar's rendering as a Hoysala memory; Bilhana's vidyapati, blue parasol and mast elephant, Kalhana's parasol (Stein VII.935-937); the Mitakshara Kalyana stanza; Lakshmadevi, the Sudi grant, the Senabhova's daughter, 130 Lokkigadyanas in 1091, Dambal 1095, Vikramapura; Itagi in Chalukya-Vikrama year 37 (September 1112), verses 65 and 67, Bennekallu, Chalukya-Rama; the children, with Mailalamahadevi's dispute disclosed; the 50th year, 3 January 1126; the later counts 52 to 94 (1127 to 1169-70). The dynasty entry's eleven rulers and years match §11.

The storytelling rule: scene prose tells events in order and with confidence; no scholar is named and no source is discussed inside a scene. The birth boon is told as the palace elders' tale with ಅಂತೆ and is not illustrated. The svayamvara is told as Bilhana reading his poem, with ಅಂತೆ. Poem-only beats (the yuvaraja refusal, the brothers' quarrel, the dreams, the Jayasimha war, the Kanchi war) are told plainly and disclosed in each scene's dramatised list. Dignity: no coup told as triumph, the elder brother seated unchained and never a villain, the grief told without the restraint, Kannegal without the emperor, Chola and Harsha mockery only on the evidence page, no 'never lost' and no superlative of the narrator's own.

Kannada: adult told-story register; no em dash; NFC; Kannada digits throughout; names consistent (ಚಂದಲದೇವಿ, ಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಾದೇವಿ, ಅಚುಗಿ, ಕಣ್ಣೆಗಾಲ, ನಡವಿಯುಪ್ಪಯನ, ಇಟಗಿ, ಲೊಕ್ಕಿಗುಂಡಿ); the English loanword ಹೆರಾಲ್ಡ್ replaced by ಘೋಷಕ. story.facts is identical to facts.json (42 facts).
illustrations: All thirteen WebPs (cover, scene-01 to scene-12, 1600x900, each under 200 KB) were opened and compared with the scene text, the alt texts, bible/style.md and its exclusions, with enlarged crops of the tower, guards, slab and faces.

The king is one man throughout and matches bible/characters/vikramaditya6-sheet.png: a broad high forehead with the hairline set back, deep-set eyes under heavy straight brows, a straight broad nose, a full short beard with a straight moustache, hair in a jewelled coil, and a medium karanda-mukuta. He is a boy in scene-01 and grey-bearded but upright in scene-12, handsome and strong in every frame. Compared with the earlier leads' covers and the Vishnuvardhana sheet (round face, upturned moustache, tall tiered cone), he is distinct.

Dignity and bible checks: the father is seen from behind in the river with no distress (03); the grief is upright (04); the captive elder brother sits unchained with his crown off, the younger stands unarmed, and the guards are in leather, not plate (06); the clemency is a hand on the kneeling brother's shoulder (08); Chandaladevi is dressed and composed at a recital, not in a harem (09); no enemy army is shown at the Narmada (10); the blue parasol goes ahead of the king's (11); the Itagi slab carries the linga, standing figures, cow and calf, sun, Nandi and moon of EI XIII p. 37 (12). No Basava, no later fort, no gunpowder and no legible Saka date appear.

Regenerated after review: scene-12, whose first render had a towering gopuram-like shrine tower; it now shows a low stepped vesara tower over lathe-turned pillars in the manner of the present Itagi temple. Nits recorded and not regenerated: background courtiers in plain white head-cloths in several frames (cover, 01, 05, 07, 09, 11), where the bible prefers gold-banded caps; conical open helmets on soldiers in scene-10; in scene-05 the boy holds his own reins, and the English alt still says the prince holds his bridle (the Kannada alt was corrected); the king has a black beard in scene-11, acceptable for about 1085.
limitations: This is an AI review by a Claude agent; no human historian or epigraphist has read the text or checked the images.

Fact checking was limited to research/kalyani-chalukya-verified.md (Fleet 1896, Bhandarkar 1896, Buhler 1875, EC VII 1902, Stein 1900, EI XIII, the SII III, XI and XX summaries, Cunningham 1894 and Elliot 1886 as read for that file), with ganga-verified.md for the 973 overthrow of the Rashtrakutas. The Kalige, Wadageri and Yedarave records, Ind. Ant. VIII, the SII XX volume and the Sanskrit text of Bilhana were not opened.
No portrait, statue or coin of Vikramaditya VI survives. All faces, the palace and hall of Kalyana, the tents, the processions and the recital are reconstructions, as the book's disclosure says.
The brothers' story, the Jayasimha war and the svayamvara rest on the victor's court poem; the book tells them as story and puts Buhler's and Bhandarkar's doubts on the last page.
Images were judged at 1600x900 WebP with enlarged crops; small distant details could not all be verified individually, and the nits above remain.
